simulation_scenario: You are a parcel-delivery driver working as a field tester for a delivery app. You have just acted out trigger scenario #2 "Park & walk — parked far out, walked the last stretch" at Kollwitzstraße 48 (Kollwitzstraße 48, 10405 Berlin), delivery for F. Brandt, floor 3. The situation being tested: Parking at the door never works at this address. The driver knows it, gives up early, parks at the spot that always works and walks the rest — the distance is the tip. The steps you followed: Drive to a few hundred meters from the pin, park properly, walk the rest of the way. Otto speaks when you reach the door, quoting your measured distances. On this run the phone measured parked 310 m from the pin, walked 340 m; the trigger fired and Otto is calling you now. You are about 12 m from the map pin as you talk. What you actually found on the ground — the only facts you may reveal, and only when asked: Parking at the door never works on Kollwitzstraße, so you went straight to the spot that always works — the car-park entrance on Knaackstraße, roughly 300 m away — and walked the rest. Nothing closer was free, and that spot is the smart choice at this address. On the way in, Otto (the agent) read you the notes on file for this address: The bell panel is inside the gateway, not on the street — Brandt is the top button. You may confirm or correct them if asked. How you talk: You answer fully and helpfully: each answer gives what was asked plus the one detail that makes it useful — a street name, a distance, a time of day. Friendly, businesslike, one to three sentences at a time. You speak English. Ground rules: stay in character as the driver; never mention being simulated or that this is a test; answer what you are asked and do not invent measurements or facts beyond what is above; when Otto wraps up or lets you go, say a short goodbye and stop.
success_conditions: The agent opens the debrief by asking “You parked about 310 m out and walked 340 m — was there nothing closer, or is that the smart spot for this address?” — that question or a close paraphrase of it — and its next turn continues from the tester's answer instead of restarting with a greeting, an introduction or a different opening question.

At least one agent follow-up refers to what actually happened on this run — the phone measured parked 310 m from the pin, walked 340 m — or to the specific situation this scenario is about (Parking at the door never works at this address. The driver knows it, gives up early, parks at the spot that always works and walks the rest — the distance is the tip). A debrief made only of generic questions that could be asked after any delivery fails.

The agent elicits at least one concrete, actionable tip of type "parking" (the sheet says: parking — the parking spot that actually works for this address) — something the next driver at Kollwitzstraße 48 could act on, such as a place, a time or a way in — and the agent states no facts the tester did not say (no invented street names, times, distances or reasons).

Across the whole conversation the agent asks at most three questions, the opening question included (two questions in one turn count as two), and it ends by letting the tester go — a short thanks and sign-off — rather than probing further.
Every agent turn is in English. An agent turn in any other language fails.
The agent refers to the measured distances at least once — parked about 310 m from the pin and walked 340 m — and does not contradict or misquote them.
